title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction
claim: Coupling a generative planner and a physics controller in a feedback loop lets execution outcomes reshape plans through alternating RL updates.
layout: 4 panels: top closed-loop pipeline, bottom-left alternation, bottom-center SFPO, bottom-right rewards
description: A dense four-part diagram. The top strip (a) shows a left-to-right loop. A prompt and goal feed a light-blue flow-matching Planner. Its generated motion goes to a green Imitation Policy controller, then to the Isaac Gym simulator, and finally to a Collected Rollout table of states, actions and rewards. Blue arrows carry the data, and a feedback line returns history states to the planner. Small humanoid renderings carrying a box appear under the arrows. An orange dashed band (b) holds the SFPO (planner), PPO (controller) and HOI Reward blocks, with yellow RL-update arrows. Below it, a left column shows Planner and Controller alternating. The center panel (c) is the SFPO diagram, with ODE-to-SDE noise injection, group compute, advantages and the objective equation. The right panel (d) is a reward-design stack. Pastel blue, green and purple mark components.
caption: Overview of InfCoiL. (a) Closed-loop framework: the flow-matching planner generates an $N_f$-frame reference window, the controller executes its first $N_r$ frames in Isaac Gym, and the realized human, object, and contact states are fed back for receding-horizon replanning. (b) Coordinated learning: controller (PPO) and planner (SFPO) training alternate \rev{to narrow the gap between planner-generated references and what the controller can execute}. (c) SFPO: \rev{for each task condition, a group of plans is sampled with semantic noise injected during denoising and executed in closed loop. Their sequence rewards are normalized within the group into relative advantages that update the planner}. (d) Reward design: the controller is trained on stepwise transition and task rewards, and each plan is scored by the time-averaged sequence reward. The interaction term is used only in open-loop controller training.
abstract: Text- and goal-conditioned human-object interaction (HOI) provides an intuitive interface for specifying high-level intents in physics-based character animation. Mapping such intents to physically plausible, contact-rich behaviors naturally calls for a generative planner and a physics-based controller, yet existing planner-controller systems either execute plans open-loop or close the loop while keeping the planner fixed, so execution feedback never reshapes what is planned. We present InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based HOI from coordinated planner-controller learning. InfCoiL couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller through a shared morphology interface in an autoregressive plan-and-execute loop, and alternately fine-tunes both components with reinforcement learning from the same physical rollouts. To optimize the flow-matching planner online, we introduce Semantic Flow Policy Optimization (SFPO), which stochasticizes selected denoising transitions with channel-wise semantic covariance over heterogeneous HOI features and assigns group-relative, sequence-level rewards from complete closed-loop executions. On held-out OMOMO sequences, InfCoiL outperforms open-loop hierarchical baselines in goal-reaching task success and physical tracking accuracy. Project page: https://infcoil.github.io/
